prompt.context: African Gold Mines Co. (AGM) is a junior gold producer with one open pit mine currently in production in Cameroon. The mine was established 10 years ago, and forecasts predict at least another 10 years of consistent gold production. Last year, AGM produced 250k oz of gold from their mine. They have come to us as their profit level has been slowly decreasing over the past five years. They had numerous operational issues with the mining equipment, problems with the workers' union and issues with community relations notably.
prompt.question: They want us to investigate what is the best course of action for their operation to return to their previous level of profitability within 12 to 24 months. They want us to specifically focus our attention on the mining department of the company.

clarifying_info.q: How much have costs changed over the past 5 years?
clarifying_info.a: Costs have increased by 20% over the past 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: What were the mining department costs in 2019?
What were the revenues for the entire company in 2019?
clarifying_info.a: Revenues for the entire company in 2019 were $375m.
The target is to return to profitability level of 5 years ago, meaning reducing costs by 20%.

exhibits.title: Revenue Structure of AGM
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing AGM's historical gold production (tonnes, left axis) and yearly average gold price ($ per ounce, right axis) from 2013 to 2019.
exhibits.data: Gold production ranges approximately 225,000–300,000 tonnes per year; gold price ranges approximately $1,000–$1,550 per ounce. Both axes are labeled with yearly data points for '13 through '19.

exhibits.title: Cost Structure of AGM Mining Department
exhibits.shows: Two charts: (1) a pie chart showing the cost breakdown of mining operations at AGM by category, and (2) a bar chart of average Brent Crude Oil Price Annually from 2010–2019, plus a table showing year-over-year cost variation (%) by category from 2015–2019.
exhibits.data: Pie chart: Equipment Maintenance 30%, Fuel 27%, Salary 28%, Overhead 10%, Other Expenses 5%. YOY cost variation table — Maintenance: 3%, 9%, 9%, 12%, 19% ('15–'19); Fuel: 3%, 3%, 5%, 9%, 13%; Salary: 1%, 0%, -2%, -1%, 1%; Overhead: 1%, 1%, 2%, 0%, 1%; Other: 1%, 5%, 5%, 0%, 0%. Brent crude oil price chart shows prices from ~$20–$120 over 2010–2019.

exhibits.title: Truck Selection Alternatives for AGM
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of five truck scenarios (current situation plus four alternatives) with CAPEX, annual maintenance cost, fuel consumption (L/hr), and expected life.
exhibits.data: Current Situation Caterpillar 777E: CAPEX $0.1m, Maintenance $540k/yr, Fuel 95 L/hr, Life 1 yr. Overhaul of Current Caterpillar 777E: CAPEX $0.6m, Maintenance $500k/yr, Fuel 80 L/hr, Life 5 yrs. New Caterpillar 777E: CAPEX $1.0m, Maintenance $340k/yr, Fuel 60 L/hr, Life 10 yrs. Komatsu HD785-7: CAPEX $1.2m, Maintenance $450k/yr, Fuel 70 L/hr, Life 12 yrs. Caterpillar 780D Autonomous Semi-Electric: CAPEX $1.6m, Maintenance $360k/yr, Fuel 40 L/hr, Life 8 yrs.

framework: Revenue branch: Price per oz x Volume (oz produced)
Cost branch: Variable costs (fuel, maintenance, salary) + Fixed costs (overhead, other)
Mining department focus: Equipment maintenance, fuel consumption, labor, overhead
Prioritize cost categories by size and rate of increase to identify biggest savings opportunity
Evaluate fleet replacement alternatives on total annual cost basis (fuel + maintenance + annualized CAPEX)
Qualitative risk/criteria assessment for shortlisted alternatives
Recommendation: choose option that meets 20% cost reduction target and passes qualitative screen

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what conclusions can you draw about revenues, and where should the investigation focus next?
questions.guidance: Revenues have remained roughly flat despite year-to-year variation in both gold price and production volume — price and volume offset each other. Gold prices are market-determined (commodity) and geology dictates annual production volume; AGM has little control over either lever. Therefore, the profitability problem is driven by rising costs, not declining revenues. The candidate should explicitly pivot the analysis to the cost side.

questions.prompt: What do you think are the biggest cost drivers in a mining operation like AGM? Which should we prioritize?
questions.guidance: Strong answers organize costs into logical buckets (e.g., variable vs. fixed, or by cost item: equipment maintenance, fuel, labor/salary, overhead, other). The candidate should then prioritize using a combination of size (% of total) and rate of growth — maintenance (30%, growing fast) and fuel (27%, growing fast) are the top two. Salary is large (28%) but nearly flat. Overhead and other are small. No prior mining knowledge is required; the logic mirrors any capital-intensive industrial operation (airlines, manufacturing).

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, identify which cost categories are driving the profitability decline and explain why.
questions.guidance: Maintenance costs (30% of total, YOY increases of 3%/9%/9%/12%/19%) and fuel costs (27%, increases of 3%/3%/5%/9%/13%) are clearly the main culprits — both large in absolute terms and accelerating rapidly. The Brent crude chart provides context for fuel but maintenance cost growth outpaces oil price movement, suggesting equipment deterioration. Salary is stable. The candidate should conclude that equipment-related costs (maintenance + fuel) are the focus area.

questions.prompt: AGM is considering replacing its truck fleet. Using Exhibit 3, calculate the total annual cost for each alternative and determine which option(s) meet the client's 20% cost reduction target.
questions.guidance: Candidate should annualize CAPEX using straight-line depreciation (CAPEX / expected life), then sum fuel cost + maintenance + annualized CAPEX. Trucks work 20 hours/day x 300 days/year = 6,000 hours/year. Fuel cost = hours x L/hr x $1/L x 20 trucks. The 20% reduction target on $36m total mining costs = savings of $7.2m. Per-truck savings x 20 trucks must exceed $7.2m. Both New Caterpillar 777E and Caterpillar 780D Autonomous Semi-Electric yield $800k/truck/year vs. $1,210k current — savings of $410k/truck x 20 = $8.2m, which exceeds the $7.2m target.

math.setup: Trucks: 20 units. Operating hours: 20 hr/day x 300 days = 6,000 hr/yr. Fuel price: $1/L. Annualized CAPEX = CAPEX / expected life. Total cost per truck = fuel cost + maintenance + annualized CAPEX.
steps: Current 777E: Fuel = 6,000 x 95 x $1 = $570k | Maintenance = $540k | CAPEX/yr = $100k/1 = $100k | Total = $1,210k/truck
Overhaul 777E: Fuel = 6,000 x 80 x $1 = $480k | Maintenance = $500k | CAPEX/yr = $600k/5 = $120k | Total = $1,100k/truck
New 777E: Fuel = 6,000 x 60 x $1 = $360k | Maintenance = $340k | CAPEX/yr = $1,000k/10 = $100k | Total = $800k/truck
Komatsu HD785-7: Fuel = 6,000 x 70 x $1 = $420k | Maintenance = $450k | CAPEX/yr = $1,200k/12 = $100k | Total = $970k/truck
Caterpillar 780D Autonomous: Fuel = 6,000 x 40 x $1 = $240k | Maintenance = $360k | CAPEX/yr = $1,600k/8 = $200k | Total = $800k/truck
Savings vs. current: New 777E and 780D Autonomous = $1,210k - $800k = $410k/truck x 20 trucks = $8.2m/yr
Target: 20% x $36m = $7.2m. Both options exceed target.
math.answer: New Caterpillar 777E and Caterpillar 780D Autonomous Semi-Electric each cost $800k/truck/year, saving $8.2m/year across the fleet — exceeding the $7.2m (20%) cost reduction target. Overhaul ($1,100k) and Komatsu ($970k) fall short.

questions.prompt: The two financially equivalent options are the New Caterpillar 777E and the Caterpillar 780D Autonomous. What qualitative criteria and risks should AGM consider when choosing between them?
questions.guidance: A Pros & Cons or criteria-based framework is appropriate. Key themes: operational continuity vs. new technology risk; remote-site feasibility; community/labor relations; environmental profile; supply chain readiness. Strong candidates acknowledge both sides and use the brainstorm to build a logical recommendation.

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative criteria and risks should AGM consider when choosing between the New Caterpillar 777E and the Caterpillar 780D Autonomous Semi-Electric?

categories.name: New Caterpillar 777E — Pros
ideas: Same model the client has been using — no learning curve
Same spare parts and supply chain already in place
Same maintenance processes — no retraining needed
Well-trained employees already familiar with operation
Longer useful life (10 years)

categories.name: New Caterpillar 777E — Cons
ideas: Possible higher wage costs if labor market tightens
Potentially higher operating costs if fuel prices rise
Requires continuous training of operators
Operational efficiency may not improve significantly

categories.name: Caterpillar 780D Autonomous — Pros
ideas: Lowest fuel consumption (40 L/hr) — larger savings if oil prices rise
Potential further cost savings if driver headcount can be reduced
Increased safety: fewer workers in dangerous areas
Potential operational efficiency gains from autonomous operation
No ongoing operator training required
Lower GHG emissions — stronger environmental profile

categories.name: Caterpillar 780D Autonomous — Cons
ideas: New technology that may be harder to implement at a remote African site
Technical support and spare parts may be difficult to obtain remotely
Maintenance and IT personnel require specialized training hard to source locally
New supply chain required; old parts inventory may be unusable
Laying off drivers in a small local community may damage community relations
Shorter useful life (8 years) vs. New 777E (10 years)
Higher upfront CAPEX ($1.6m vs. $1.0m per truck)

recommendation: AGM's profitability decline is driven primarily by rapidly rising equipment maintenance and fuel costs in the mining department, not by revenue weakness.

To return to previous profitability levels, AGM should replace its fleet of 20 Caterpillar 777E trucks with either the New Caterpillar 777E or the Caterpillar 780D Autonomous Semi-Electric — both reduce annual fleet costs by $8.2m, exceeding the $7.2m (20%) target.
If continuity and remote-site feasibility are prioritized, the New Caterpillar 777E is recommended: same model, same supply chain, minimal disruption, 10-year life.

If AGM is willing to manage the implementation complexity, the 780D Autonomous offers additional upside — further savings if fuel prices rise, safety improvements, and environmental benefits — though community relations around potential job losses must be managed carefully.
risks: For 780D Autonomous: technology implementation risk in a remote location with limited technical infrastructure
For 780D Autonomous: community backlash if autonomous trucks lead to driver layoffs in a small Cameroonian village where AGM is a major employer
For both options: construction, delivery, and transition period may temporarily disrupt production
Fuel price assumptions ($1/L) may change; Komatsu and 780D options become more attractive if oil prices rise significantly
next_steps: Conduct detailed implementation feasibility study for the chosen truck model, including logistics to remote Cameroon site
Engage with the workers' union early to manage labor transition, especially if autonomous trucks are selected
Negotiate fleet procurement contract to lock in pricing and delivery schedule
Establish new maintenance and supply chain agreements with the chosen supplier
Set milestone reviews at 6 and 12 months post-implementation to track cost reduction progress against the 20% target
